logic_node.action_detail: In patients with suspected or new-onset HF, or those presenting with acute decompensated HF, a chest x-ray should be performed to assess heart size and pulmonary congestion and to detect alternative cardiac, pulmonary, and other diseases that may cause or contribute to symptoms.

source_text: In patients with suspected or new-onset HF, or those presenting with acute decompensated HF, a chest x-ray should be performed to assess heart size and pulmonary congestion and to detect alternative cardiac, pulmonary, and other diseases that may cause or contribute to the patient's symptoms.

logic_node.action_detail: In patients with suspected or newly diagnosed HF, transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) should be performed during initial evaluation to assess cardiac structure and function.

source_text: In patients with suspected or newly diagnosed HF, transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) should be performed during initial evaluation to assess cardiac structure and function.

logic_node.action: Repeat echocardiography for clinical change or pre-procedure evaluation
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF who have had a significant clinical change, or who have received GDMT and are being considered for invasive procedures or device therapy, repeat measurement of EF, degree of structural remodeling, and valvular function are useful to inform therapeutic interventions. Reevaluation of EF recommended >40 days after MI, >90 days after revascularization, >90 days after GDMT.

source_text: In patients with HF who have had a significant clinical change, or who have received GDMT and are being considered for invasive procedures or device therapy, repeat measurement of EF, degree of structural remodeling, and valvular function are useful.

logic_node.action: Use alternative imaging when echocardiography is inadequate
logic_node.action_detail: In patients for whom echocardiography is inadequate, alternative imaging (cardiac magnetic resonance [CMR], cardiac computed tomography [CT], radionuclide imaging) is recommended for assessment of LVEF.

source_text: In patients for whom echocardiography is inadequate, alternative imaging (eg, cardiac magnetic resonance [CMR], cardiac computed tomography [CT], radionuclide imaging) is recommended for assessment of LVEF.

logic_node.action: Consider CMR for HF or cardiomyopathy diagnosis and management
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF or cardiomyopathy, CMR can be useful for diagnosis or management. CMR provides noninvasive myocardial characterization including late-gadolinium enhancement for fibrosis detection and T1/T2 mapping for infiltrative and inflammatory cardiomyopathies (myocarditis, sarcoidosis, Fabry disease, amyloidosis).

source_text: In patients with HF or cardiomyopathy, CMR can be useful for diagnosis or management.

logic_node.action: Evaluate for ischemic heart disease as cause of HF
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF, an evaluation for possible ischemic heart disease can be useful to identify the cause and guide management. Noninvasive stress imaging with echocardiography or nuclear scintigraphy can identify patients likely to have obstructive CAD. Invasive or CT coronary angiography can detect and characterize extent of CAD.

source_text: In patients with HF, an evaluation for possible ischemic heart disease can be useful to identify the cause and guide management.

logic_node.action: Consider noninvasive stress imaging to guide coronary revascularization
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF and coronary artery disease (CAD) who are candidates for coronary revascularization, noninvasive stress imaging (stress echocardiography, SPECT, CMR, or PET) may be considered for detection of myocardial ischemia to help guide coronary revascularization decisions.

source_text: In patients with HF and coronary artery disease (CAD) who are candidates for coronary revascularization, noninvasive stress imaging (stress echocardiography, SPECT, CMR, or PET) may be considered for detection of myocardial ischemia.

logic_node.action: Do not perform routine repeat LV function assessment without indication
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF, in the absence of: 1) clinical status change, 2) treatment interventions that might have had a significant effect on cardiac function, or 3) candidacy for invasive procedures or device therapy, routine repeat assessment of LV function is not indicated.
